tagline: The Arcane theme that took League of Legends to the Hot 100.
headline: Imagine Dragons and JID gave Arcane its theme, and it became the top track on League's Spotify page.
summary: Released on October 28, 2021, Imagine Dragons and JID's "Enemy" became the theme of Arcane, Riot Games' first animated series, and opened every episode of both seasons outside China. It peaked at No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100, topped Pop Airplay and Alternative Airplay, is 4× Platinum in the US and has passed 2 billion Spotify streams, far more than any other track on League of Legends' Spotify page. The band behind Worlds 2014's "Warriors" also brought it to the Worlds 2021 stage, in an Arcane-themed Show Open that aired on the day the series premiered.

story.heading: Written years before anyone saw Zaun
story.body:
*Enemy* started long before *Arcane* had a release date. Imagine Dragons had been League fans and Riot collaborators since writing *Warriors* for Worlds 2014. In Riot's documentary series *Arcane: Bridging the Rift*, Dan Reynolds recalls co-creator Christian Linke showing him slides and storyboards while the show was still at a very early stage. Even that was enough for him to understand the push and pull between the sisters Vi and Jinx. In Riot Games Music's making-of video, the band says Riot showed them early sketches years before release and that they started writing from there. GRAMMY.com later reported that about four years passed between the song's writing and its release.

In the single's press release, Reynolds described *Enemy* as a song about reconciling internal conflict when it feels impossible to trust even yourself, and in *Bridging the Rift* he says it was written from a feeling of isolation, you against the world. The band wrote it with Justin Tranter and the Swedish duo Mattman & Robin, who produced it; Serban Ghenea mixed it. The rap verse came late. Once the song was finished, Reynolds suggested JID and cut his own vocal from the bridge to make room. JID said the opening lines of his verse came from a song he had started with Mac Miller, who told him they would fit better on this track. Gizmodo reported that the band was among the artists who fought with their labels to be part of the *Arcane* soundtrack.

The song is musically unusual too. ONE Esports points out that it runs on just two chords and never plays its home chord of B minor. That unresolved tension suits a show about a family coming apart.

story.heading: Arcane's front door
story.body:
*Enemy* came out on October 28, 2021, as the lead single from the *Arcane* soundtrack. An animated music video premiered on the League of Legends YouTube channel the same day, nine days before the series reached Netflix. Fortiche, the studio behind *Arcane*, made it with co-directors Arnaud Delord and Bart Maunoury. Before the show aired, the video previewed its central story: Powder's childhood in Zaun, her bond with Vi, the sisters' falling-out and her slide toward becoming Jinx. Imagine Dragons appear as Zaunites themselves, playing cards in an undercity bar, and JID turns up in the same bar for his verse.

*Arcane*, Riot's first TV series, arrived on November 6, 2021, in three weekly acts. *Enemy* played over the opening titles of every episode and turned up again inside episode five. In China, the series used a different opening theme, Eason Chan's *Lonely Warrior*. The show reached No. 1 on Netflix's Top 10 in 52 countries. In November 2021, *Enemy* topped Billboard's Top TV Songs chart with 25.7 million U.S. on-demand streams that month, and two more *Arcane* songs, Bea Miller's *Playground* and Ramsey's *Goodbye*, also made the list.

story.heading: Worlds 2021: the night Arcane arrived
story.body:
Seven years after *Warriors*, Imagine Dragons came back to Worlds. Edward Gaming and DWG KIA played the 2021 final on November 6 at Laugardalshöll in Reykjavík. Because of the pandemic there was no live audience, and the final went out hours before *Arcane* premiered. Riot's Show Open told an Arcane story. Vi searches the undercity while Jinx watches her, Bea Miller sings *Playground*, Imagine Dragons and JID perform *Enemy* on a smoky Zaun street, and PVRIS and Denzel Curry close with the Worlds anthem *Burn It All Down*. Guinness World Records lists that final's peak audience as 73,860,742 concurrent viewers.

It almost looked very different. In Riot's documentary on the Show Open, the team explains that the original plan was a huge live stage show in a stadium in mainland China, bigger than Beijing's Bird's Nest. On August 16, 2021 it became clear that could not happen, and Worlds moved to Iceland. The team rebuilt the ceremony as a 13½-minute cinematic in less than two months. It used music videos already shot in Los Angeles and a 360-degree Zaun set built in Birmingham, England, and more than 1,300 people worked on it. The first sequence finished was the arcade scene with Jinx and Vi that links *Playground* and *Enemy*, completed on the Wednesday before the Saturday broadcast. The team expected to deliver the finished Show Open only about two hours before air.

story.heading: From the Rift to the Hot 100
story.body:
*Enemy* kept climbing long after the premiere. In January 2022 it reached No. 1 on Billboard's Rock Streaming Songs chart. That gave Imagine Dragons five No. 1s there, the most in the chart's history. The song entered the Hot 100's top 10 in March and peaked at No. 5 on the chart dated April 9, 2022. It was JID's first US top-5 hit and the band's first since *Thunder* in 2017. On May 7 it reached No. 1 on Billboard's Pop Airplay chart. It also spent nine weeks at No. 1 on Alternative Airplay during a 54-week run and peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard Global 200.

The song finished 2022 at No. 15 on the Hot 100 year-end chart and No. 9 on the Global 200. Billboard later ranked it 14th on its all-time Alternative Airplay list. It is certified 4× Platinum in the US, Diamond in France and Poland, and 3× Diamond in Brazil. It also won awards: two 2022 Clio Music awards, for the video's animation and for the Riot partnership, LOS40's Best International Song, and the 2023 iHeartRadio Music Award for Alternative Song of the Year. It was also nominated at the MTV VMAs and the American Music Awards.

story.heading: On every big stage
story.body:
For a song born from a game, *Enemy* travelled far. Imagine Dragons and JID performed it at the MTV Europe Music Awards in Budapest on November 14, 2021, and at The Game Awards in Los Angeles on December 9. The band's upload of The Game Awards performance has about 26.7 million views, more than three times the Worlds clip. Rolling Stone noted that the band played the song more than 70 times on its 2022 tour. JID joined only for a handful of big moments, including a March 2022 Mercury Tour show in Los Angeles. At the 2022 American Music Awards, where *Enemy* was up for Favorite Rock Song, the band went from *Bones* straight into *Enemy* and JID closed it out.

The band stayed part of League's community, too. In *Bridging the Rift*, Reynolds says Vi is the champion he plays. He also admits the band has been late on stage because they were finishing a ranked game and didn't want to be banned. In December 2021, LevelUp reported that he had joined streamer Midbeast for some League games and sang the *Enemy* chorus while they waited for a match to start.

story.heading: Two billion streams
story.body:
On Spotify, *Enemy* is far ahead of every other track on League of Legends' artist page. The single version with JID, which appears on both Imagine Dragons' and League of Legends' artist pages, has passed 2.06 billion streams. That is about 2.6 times *Legends Never Die*, the next track on the League page, and more than double Imagine Dragons' own *Warriors* (about 880 million). It is the band's fifth most-streamed song, behind only *Believer*, *Demons*, *Thunder* and *Radioactive* and ahead of *Bones* and *Whatever It Takes*. A separate version credited to Imagine Dragons alone has about 415 million more.

On YouTube, the music video has about 370 million views and 3.9 million likes. Among the music videos in this archive, only K/DA's *POP/STARS*, *Warriors* and *RISE* have more views.

story.heading: The opening nobody wanted to change
story.body:
When *Arcane* returned for its second and final season on November 9, 2024, it kept *Enemy* as its theme instead of following the anime habit of a new opening each season. Christian Linke told ONE Esports that he had wanted to replace it, but colleagues pushed back. He came around to the idea that the song's emotional pull mattered, comparing it to the way the *Dragon Ball* music is fixed in fans' memories, and executive producer Alex Yee said the goal was for the opening to feel "like putting on your jacket." Fortiche redrew the title sequence with the same characters, now in simple, muted clothes under soft sunset light.

*Enemy (Opening Title Version)* came out on November 23, 2024, the day the final act was released, as the closing track of the Season 2 soundtrack, with an official visualizer on Riot Games Music's channel. It is the arrangement heard over the show's titles, more orchestral and slightly longer. Gizmodo noted that orchestral strings and trumpets take over from the original's backing and that a ticking clock runs under JID's verse, and argued that the release brought the band's relationship with Riot full circle. *Arcane* itself won the Emmy for Outstanding Animated Program in 2022, the first streaming series to do so, and won it again in 2025. Every one of its episodes opened with *Enemy*.

whyItMatters: It is the theme of Arcane, Riot's first TV series, and opened every episode of both seasons (2021 and 2024) outside China.

It took League-related music deep into the mainstream: No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100, No. 3 on the Global 200, No. 1 on Pop Airplay, nine weeks at No. 1 on Alternative Airplay and 4× Platinum in the US.
With more than 2 billion Spotify streams, it is the top track on League of Legends' Spotify page, about 2.6× Legends Never Die and more than double Warriors.
It brought Imagine Dragons back to Worlds seven years after Warriors, in an Arcane-themed Show Open that aired on the day the series premiered.
Its Fortiche-animated video (about 370M views) introduced Jinx's backstory before the show aired and won two Clio Music awards.
Imagine Dragons and JID took it to the MTV EMAs, The Game Awards and the American Music Awards, and it won iHeartRadio's Alternative Song of the Year.

keyMoments.label: The band in Zaun
keyMoments.description: Imagine Dragons, drawn in Fortiche's Arcane style, sit around a card table in a lamplit undercity bar.

keyMoments.label: Title card
keyMoments.description: The word ENEMY flickers through changing graffiti lettering over young Powder and her wind-up monkey toy.

keyMoments.label: Sisters
keyMoments.description: Vi holds a sobbing Powder, the bond the rest of the video pulls apart.

keyMoments.label: First chorus
keyMoments.description: The first chorus lands while Powder, Vi and their gang horse around in their undercity hideout.

keyMoments.label: Second chorus
keyMoments.description: The band's frontman, drawn as a tattooed Zaunite, sings the second chorus in close-up.

keyMoments.label: The falling-out
keyMoments.description: Vi pulls away from a pleading Powder and leaves, the break the Arcane story turns on.

keyMoments.label: JID's verse
keyMoments.description: JID appears in the bar with glowing eyes, and the Zaun palette shatters into neon pop-art as his verse begins.

keyMoments.label: Final chorus
keyMoments.description: The last chorus hits as slashes of neon red tear across Powder and a glaring eye.

keyMoments.label: Jinx looms
keyMoments.description: A giant close-up of Jinx's glare fills the screen, then she rises out of the dark behind young Powder.

keyMoments.label: Powder becomes Jinx
keyMoments.description: Powder's face glitches and turns into Jinx's, the transformation the whole video builds toward.

keyMoments.label: Arcane
keyMoments.description: After a last look at the band in the bar and the Riot Games logo, the video ends on the Arcane: League of Legends title card.

keyMoments.label: Jinx watches Vi
keyMoments.description: Vi searches a Zaun hideout while Jinx watches from the shadows, then neon graffiti monsters burst to life behind Vi.

keyMoments.label: Dan Reynolds on the balcony
keyMoments.description: Dan Reynolds leans over a wrought-iron balcony on the Zaun street set.

keyMoments.label: The band on a Zaun street
keyMoments.description: The band plays at the end of a smoky Zaun street lit by green neon.

keyMoments.label: JID's verse
keyMoments.description: JID, eyes glowing green, raps his verse in a Zaun backroom.

keyMoments.label: Vi finds Jinx
keyMoments.description: In a dark room lit by a glowing hextech sphere, Vi and Jinx come face to face.

keyMoments.label: The sisters collide
keyMoments.description: The sisters' clash erupts in red laser fire and a burst of blue hextech energy.

keyMoments.label: Where Enemy began
keyMoments.description: The band explains that Riot showed them early Arcane sketches years before the series came out, and that they started writing from there.

keyMoments.label: Plans collapse
keyMoments.description: Riot recalls August 16, 2021, when it became clear that the planned stadium ceremony in mainland China could not go ahead.

keyMoments.label: Down to the wire
keyMoments.description: The team reveals that the Jinx-and-Vi arcade scene linking Playground and Enemy was the first sequence finished, on the Wednesday before the Saturday broadcast.

keyMoments.label: Inside the band's studio
keyMoments.description: Dan Reynolds shows the studio where Enemy was made, says Vi is his League champion and recalls Christian Linke's early Arcane storyboards.

featuredClip.description: In the final chorus, Jinx's glare fills the frame, she rises behind young Powder in the dark, and Powder's face glitches into Jinx's.
